rules: Label only what the website states. No outside knowledge. Copy quotes exactly. If pages disagree, record both as conflicting. If the site does not say, use not_found.
review_notes: Headquarters marked not_found: the About Us page states Thoughtworks was 'established in Chicago in 1993' and operates '47 offices across 18 countries' as a distributed multinational, but never designates a current single HQ; the office-locations page lists many addresses (New York, San Francisco, Chicago, etc.) with none labeled headquarters. 'Great Place to Work-Certified' was excluded from traction.certifications as an employer-branding award rather than a compliance/security certification. traction.partnerships evidence is a single shared quote from the partnerships page since individual per-company quotes weren't distinctly captured beyond category groupings. No page found where Thoughtworks names a specific competitor (its 'Why Thoughtworks is Different' post explicitly avoids naming competitors, only naming Google once as an unrelated scale comparison, not as a competitor). B-51 (2026-09-27): customers.segments was previously marked 'inferred' (also structurally unmatchable, since this field isn't on INFERENCE_WHITELIST) and its evidence was actually the industries list duplicated from customers.industries, not a distinct customer-TYPE statement; re-checked live and found a genuine segment-type sentence on the clients page ('from high-growth scale-ups to Fortune 500 enterprises') distinguishing company size/maturity as its own claim -- corrected status to 'extracted' and evidence to that real quote, dropping the industry-vertical elaboration which correctly belongs only under customers.industries.
